In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(a) the regional variability of heavy metals in soils is controlled by parent rocks; (b) the anthropic impact, although present and detectable, is not yet a major factor controlling the variability; and (c) the anthropic contribution is more relevant for Pb than for the other metals.

the use of multivariate statistic and GIS-based approaches is a useful tool for the identification of the main factors controlling the regional heavy metal distribution, for the identification of possible non-point sources, and for the definition of background values and realistic guidelines.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the regional geochemical background values for heavy metals in soils should be defined on the basis of a regional database, which includes the geological setting, the land use and the anthropic activities.

the knowledge of the background values, and of the natural and anthropic origin of potentially harmful elements in the soil is a fundamental step to define realistic mandatory guidelines for agricultural soils.

the knowledge of the regional background values and the natural vs. anthropic origin for potentially harmful metals in soils, is of critical importance for the assessment of human impact and for the fixing of guide values and quality standard.
